definition: Source-reported views. Shorts changed to starts/replays on 2025-03-31. Official all-format first-frame counting rollout announced starting 2026-08-24; this channel retention UI explicitly says views counted differently from 2026-08-27. Preserve both evidence dates; do not impose a single inferred historical breakpoint.
Source-reported engaged views; click/tap to watch or playback beyond initial seconds. Keep separate from total views.
Source watch time in hours. Retained without silently changing units.
Duration parsed from the native h:mm:ss value. Core average uses engaged metrics. Do not average row averages.
Source average percentage viewed in percentage points, not a fraction. Replay can make this exceed 100%; retain the reported value without capping. Do not add or average unweighted.
Source net subscriber change over the selected period, not subscriber balance.
Source subscriber gains over the selected period.
Source subscriber losses over the selected period; positive number of losses.
Source likes metric for the selected reporting period.
Source dislikes metric for the selected reporting period.
Source shares metric for the selected reporting period.
Source comments added metric for the selected reporting period.
Eligible thumbnail impressions, not total video exposure across every surface.
Source thumbnail CTR in percent units. Preserve reported denominator/scope; do not derive from all views.
Estimated distinct audience within this exact report window (up to 90 days). Do not sum across videos, dates, or overlapping scopes.
Source estimated returning viewers in the selected reporting window.
Source estimated new viewers in the selected reporting window.
Source-reported average views per viewer. Preserve source numerator definition; do not infer unique people from view-segment counts.
Source percentage distribution of views within the report population.
Source percentage distribution of watch time within the report population.
